node.title: Re^3: Embedded Newlines or Converting One-Liner to Loop
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [mwb613],

I second [mod://Text::CSV] as "the" solution for reading CSV files, especially if they've got things like embedded newlines. It would also help in the case that the input format changes, since [mod://Text::CSV] is quite flexible.

my log processor doesn't just work with CSVs but I think I can probably work around that

One solution would be to abstract out the handling of records, so that it doesn't matter where they come from:

my $csv = Text::CSV->new({ binary => 1, eol => $/ }) or die Text::CSV->error_diag; open my $fh, "<", $file or die "$file: $!"; while ( my $row = $csv->getline($fh) ) { handle_row($row); } $csv->eof or $csv->error_diag(); close $fh; sub handle_row { # ... }

(Untested, mostly a copy-n-paste from [mod://Text::CSV].)

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
